title: Uniform numberings of oracle programs

based_on.title: Computability theory
based_on.pages: §15.1, printed/PDF p. 63: uniform oracle enumeration, parameterization and relativization; version 2024-02-25

summary: Build one evaluator and one parameter map that work for every oracle, then characterize relative enumerable sets by finite certificate tests.
abstract: Giving a program access to membership answers should not require rewriting its instructions whenever the answering set changes. Numbering the finite query programs makes this precise: one fixed evaluator runs any indexed program with whichever oracle is supplied. It finds halting results by repeatedly checking larger finite resource allowances, while a computation with no result remains undefined. A terminating transformation can also insert fixed numerical inputs into program text without asking the oracle any questions. These uniform constructions distinguish building a program from running it, and explain how membership recognized with an oracle has finite certificates whose checks may still need that oracle. Racing two such recognizers gives a decision procedure exactly when they recognize complementary sets.
